biography.plain_text: Cyrus Mistry was an Irish businessman who chaired Tata Sons from 2012 to 2016. A civil engineering graduate of Imperial College London, he previously led the construction business of his family’s Shapoorji Pallonji Group. He later co-founded Mistry Ventures with his brother Shapoor, investing in and advising businesses across sectors.

long_biography.plain_text:
Businessman Cyrus Mistry helped his family’s construction group work through a major debt restructuring. Although he no longer sat on the flagship company’s board, he helped arrange asset sales and the disposal of stakes in other businesses. Working with his brother, he followed through on the repayment programme, enabling the group to leave the restructuring scheme in 2022.

He mentored marketing professor Nirmalya Kumar, a member of his group executive council, and allowed him to challenge decisions in front of colleagues. Kumar worked on strategy during Mistry’s leadership of the Tata group.
